title: nnU-Net for Brain Tumor Segmentation (region-based training)
mechanism: Replace the softmax over exclusive labels with per-region sigmoid outputs and BCE + Dice on nested, overlapping regions that match the evaluation regions.
adaptation: Keep the 24-class softmax for the other classes. Add 3 sigmoid channels. D = crack OR inactive (the damaged area). I = inactive, hole-filled, so it includes crack pixels inside it. C = crack, kept even inside inactive. Inference: softmax argmax, then overwrite with I > t_I, then C > t_C, with thresholds chosen on val or fold CV. D is a large, easy target that shares features between the two rare classes. This frees the 20% of crack pixels that argmax currently gives to inactive.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + D/I/C sigmoid channels with overlap targets. Baseline: PF (5 seeds). Metrics: inactive IoU on module-grouped 5-fold CV and on clean 49, crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill if the CV inactive IoU gain is < 0.02 and crack IoU falls by more than 0.012.
evidence: R (tables 1 and 2 of the PDF): 5-fold CV mean Dice 86.09 -> 86.73 with region training (tumour core +1.0, enhancing +2.0). Validation 83.76 -> 84.13. 369 training cases, 3D MRI.
prior_overlap: none. BRIEF section 5 lists multi-label heads as never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Keep 24-class softmax; add 3 sigmoid channels D = crack OR inactive, I = inactive hole-filled, C = crack kept inside inactive (recover crack layer under inactive from 2022 correction layers or mask the loss there). Final map: argmax, then write I, then C (outer to inner) with val/CV thresholds.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + D/I/C sigmoid heads (BCE+Dice), 5 seeds + module-grouped 5-fold CV; baseline PF; metrics inactive IoU (CV and clean 49), crack IoU, relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU; kill if inactive CV IoU gain < 0.02 and crack IoU drop > 0.012.
